There's a new paper (https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.21852) showing that eml(x, y) = exp(x) - log(y) with constant 1 is a universal generator for elementary functions, analogous to NAND for Boolean logic. The construction chain relies on identities like log 0 = -∞ and exp(-∞) = 0.

Naturally, this breaks in Lean because Complex.log 0 = 0. The author comments this explicitly in the paper. This got me thinking about whether there's a clean way to handle this in Mathlib. Anyone's got any ideas? The broader question of course is whether a single-operator basis for elementary functions would be useful in Mathlib at all, or whether it's a curiosity that won't actually compress proof work.
I guess you'd need an docs#EReal.log here (extended with junk values from docs#ENNReal.log)

As far as I can see this has nothing to do with Lean -- what is log(-1)? This eml function has subtraction so must be allowing negative numbers, and yet log(-1) is undefined. I think that's a far bigger problem than log(0). It's not difficult to write down formal combinations of eml which make sense nowhere. If you allow EReal then you have the problem of figuring out what infinity-infinity is supposed to be. I cannot see these sorts of issues being treated anywhere in the paper.
Someone on this Zulip claims to have formalised this precise paper
See #mathlib4 > Formalization of EML Sheffer operator paper arXiv:2603.21852 @ 💬
I thought the EMF construction required complex functions, but if so then the constructions given for x - y and x - (y + 2 pi i) would give the same result...

Eric Wieser disse:

I guess you'd need an docs#EReal.log here (extended with junk values from docs#ENNReal.log)

If it's restricted to a sub-type with only float-values this could work, part of his strategy in the paper is doing exactly that. It probably opens the door to other problems though.
I highly doubt that eml(x, y) is an accurate universal generator for IEEE 754 floats
